On 17 February 2009, following clashes within the party and only a day after a heavy defeat of the PD in the 2009 Sardinian regional election,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-18) Veltroni announced his immediate resignation from his leadership post.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-bbc_veltroni_resignations-1) The Constituent Assembly of the party subsequently convened on 21 February 2009 and elected Veltroni's former deputy Dario Franceschini as the new secretary.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-19)
On 28 September 2014, in Venice,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-Sky-Wedded-2014-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-USAToday-Wedded-2014-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-CorrieredellaSera-WedLeak-2014-22) Veltroni officiated the wedding of George Clooney and Amal Alamuddin.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-CorrieredellaSera-WedLeak-2014-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-Telegraph-exRomeMayor-2014-23) The wedding was widely reported in the media.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-Telegraph-WeddingEnds-2014-24)

**Virginia Elena Raggi** (Italian pronunciation:[[virˈdʒiːnja ˈraddʒi]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); born 18 July 1978) is an Italian lawyer and politician who served as Mayor of Rome from 2016 to 2021. A member of the anti-establishment Five Star Movement (M5S), Raggi was first elected to the Rome city council in 2013. Raggi led her party to victory in the 2016 municipal election, becoming the first woman and first M5S member elected mayor of Rome.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Guardian2-1) Following the defeat of the M5S in the 2021 Rome municipal election, Raggi left office as mayor.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-:0-2)
texts.1: Raggi was born and raised in the Appio-Latino quarter of Rome, and studied law at the Roma Tre University, specialising in judicial and extrajudicial civil law.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Gazebo-3) Despite not having any prior political experience, she credits the birth of her son for sparking her involvement in politics.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-:0-2) She was previously a member of local neighborhood boards before joining the Five Star Movement for Rome district XIV in 2011.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-penta-4) At the time of her election Raggi lived with her family in Ottavia[it] in Northern Rome.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Gazebo-3) She is married to fellow M5S member Andrea Severini with whom she has one child, born in 2009.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Gazebo-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-theage-5)

## Rome City Council and the 2016 election
[edit]
In the 2013 municipal election, Raggi was one of four members of the Five Star Movement elected to Rome city council.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Guardian1-6) The maximum term of office lasts five years, but the resignation of mayor Ignazio Marino (a member of the Democratic Party) triggered early elections; Marino was ousted from office after more than half the city's councillors stepped down.
Raggi won the closed primary (against Marcello De Vito — the party's 2013 nominee to the office of mayor — and other minor candidates) in preparation for the upcoming June 2016 Rome municipal early election.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Guardian1-6) Described by _The Economist_ as "a talented debater",[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-7) Raggi is the first female mayor of the city. She "promised to fight corruption and bring back Rome's splendor a year after a wide-reaching scandal exposed criminal infiltration in city bidding contracts".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-8) Raggi opposed the Rome bid for the 2024 Summer Olympics arguing that the city was in a "delicate moment"[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-9) pointing out the spiralling deficits in Olympic cities.

## Rome City Council and the 2016 election
Raggi and her party (Five Star Movement, M5S) came in first place in the first round of voting (5 June 2016) in the Rome mayoral election, garnering over 35 percent of the vote.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-theage-5) In the second round of voting (19 June 2016), Raggi opposed Roberto Giachetti, a member of the Democratic Party (PD) and Vice President of the Chamber of Deputies in the XVII Legislature, who obtained over 24 percent of the vote in first round. Raggi won the second round with 67.2 percent of or slightly over 770,000 votes;[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-10) she is the first woman and the first member of M5S to hold the office of Mayor of Rome.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Guardian2-1)
Virginia Raggi during a public speech as mayor of Rome
One of Raggi's first acts as mayor was the withdrawal of the 2024 Olympic bid stating that "with 13 billion euros in debt, Rome can't afford taking on more debt to make cathedrals in the desert".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Dampf-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Olympic_bid-12) Raggi's decision also crippled the Italian bid to host the 2023 Rugby World Cup. FIR's (Italian rugby federation) bid, indeed, relied on IOC's financial contribution to the renewal of the venues which would have hosted the Olympics' football tournament and that would have been seat also of the Rugby World Cup (except for Verona, substituted by Padua). After Raggi's withdrawal of the bid, FIR president Alfredo Gavazzi announced that there were no longer the conditions to keep on supporting the Italian bid for the World Cup.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-13)

**Walter Veltroni**OMRI (Italian pronunciation:[[ˈvalter velˈtroːni]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); born 3 July 1955) is an Italian writer, film director, journalist and politician. He served as the first leader of the Democratic Party within the Italian centre-left opposition until his resignation on 17 February 2009.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-bbc_veltroni_resignations-1) He also served as mayor of Rome from June 2001 to February 2008.

## Early life and family
[edit]
Veltroni was born in Rome. His father, Vittorio Veltroni, an eminent RAI manager in the 1950s, died one year after his birth.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-2) His mother, Ivanka Kotnik, was the daughter of Ciril Kotnik, a Slovenian diplomat at the Holy See who helped numerous Jews and anti-fascists to escape Nazi persecution after 1943.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-3)
Veltroni joined the Italian Communist Youth Federation (FGCI) at the age of 15, and was elected Rome city councillor in 1976 as a member of the Italian Communist Party (PCI), serving until 1981. He was then elected to the Chamber of Deputies in 1987. As a member of the PCI's national secretariat in 1988, he played a leading role in the transformation into a social democratic party._[citation needed_]

## Early life and family
Veltroni, a professional journalist, was editor-in-chief of _[L'Unità](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'Unit%C3%A0 "L'Unità")_, the newspaper of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) from 1992 to 1996. He then ran as one of the leading members of The Olive Tree coalition in the 1996 Italian general election. After The Olive Tree's victory, he served as Deputy Prime Minister of Italy and Minister for Cultural Assets and Activities from 1996 to 1998, joining 25 other PDS members in the cabinet, which was the first former PCI members to take part in government since 1947. Also in 1996, he joined the Bilderberg Meeting. In 1998, he resigned, subsequent to his election as National Secretary of the Democrats of the Left (DS). Despite his background as a journalist, he has been involved in controversial episodes related to freedom of expression. For example, in 2001, after the late-night show _Satyricon_ aired an interview that discussed indictments on links between the right-wing leader and the mafia, Marco Travaglio reported that Veltroni dispatched a messenger menacing the closure of the show.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-4)

## Early life and family
In 2001, Veltroni resigned as leader of the party after being elected mayor of Rome. In May 2006, Veltroni was confirmed mayor of Rome, easily defeating Gianni Alemanno, a former Minister of Agriculture and then a member of National Alliance, obtaining an unprecedented 61.4% of the valid votes against the 37.1% achieved by Alemanno. The percentage of votes that supported Veltroni's second term in office was a record in local elections in Rome. Shortly before this confirmation, Veltroni had declared that he was going to leave politics at the end of his second term as mayor._[citation needed_] In 2005, as mayor of Rome, he met in Washington during a visit to the United States the then United States senator Barack Obama,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-5) being one of his earliest supporters overseas.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-6) He wrote the preface to the Italian edition of _The Audacity of Hope_ in 2007,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-7) and has been referred to as "Obama's European counterpart".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-8)

## Early life and family
By 2007, Veltroni was widely considered one of the most popular centre-left politicians in Italy, and often singled out for the leadership of the Democratic Party (PD), despite his statements that he would not accept such position after his tenure as mayor would end. In June 2007, DS leader Piero Fassino publicly asked Veltroni to run for the party leadership, offering support from all of his party. Several other PD leading members publicly stated their support for a possible candidacy of Veltroni. Furthermore, the strongest of his possible contenders, Pier Luigi Bersani, which polls showed as having a 50% support in regions of Central and Northern Italy,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-9) withdrew to avoid a "confusing candidacy".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-10) Veltroni officially presented his candidacy for the leadership of the PD at a rally in Turin on 27 June 2007. At this occasion, he introduced the four key issues his programme would address: environment, generational pact, education, and public security.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-11)

Veltroni during the electoral campaign in April 2008
Veltroni was elected as the first leader of the newly founded PD on 14 October 2007, winning an open primary with around 2.6 million votes, or 75.8%.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-12) In 2007, Veltroni had some remarks against the Romanian immigrants, claiming that Italy has become "unlivable" since Romania joined the European Union,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-13) while before its entry Rome was "the safest city in the world", bringing accusations of xenophobia from the Romanian press.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-14)
Following the 2008 Italian political crisis that led to the defeat of Romano Prodi's government in a January vote in the Senate of the Republic,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-15) Veltroni led the PD into the 2008 Italian general election on 13–14 April 2008. Veltroni resigned as mayor of Rome on 13 February 2008 to concentrate on the campaign.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-16) He was criticized for his over-frequentation of Rome socialites and was advised to focus on more practical problems.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Veltroni#cite_note-17)

**Virginia Elena Raggi** (Italian pronunciation:[[virˈdʒiːnja ˈraddʒi]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); born 18 July 1978) is an Italian lawyer and politician who served as Mayor of Rome from 2016 to 2021. A member of the anti-establishment Five Star Movement (M5S), Raggi was first elected to the Rome city council in 2013. Raggi led her party to victory in the 2016 municipal election, becoming the first woman and first M5S member elected mayor of Rome.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Guardian2-1) Following the defeat of the M5S in the 2021 Rome municipal election, Raggi left office as mayor.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-:0-2)

Raggi was born and raised in the Appio-Latino quarter of Rome, and studied law at the Roma Tre University, specialising in judicial and extrajudicial civil law.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Gazebo-3) Despite not having any prior political experience, she credits the birth of her son for sparking her involvement in politics.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-:0-2) She was previously a member of local neighborhood boards before joining the Five Star Movement for Rome district XIV in 2011.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-penta-4) At the time of her election Raggi lived with her family in Ottavia[it] in Northern Rome.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Gazebo-3) She is married to fellow M5S member Andrea Severini with whom she has one child, born in 2009.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Gazebo-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-theage-5)

## Rome City Council and the 2016 election

In the 2013 municipal election, Raggi was one of four members of the Five Star Movement elected to Rome city council.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Guardian1-6) The maximum term of office lasts five years, but the resignation of mayor Ignazio Marino (a member of the Democratic Party) triggered early elections; Marino was ousted from office after more than half the city's councillors stepped down.
Raggi won the closed primary (against Marcello De Vito — the party's 2013 nominee to the office of mayor — and other minor candidates) in preparation for the upcoming June 2016 Rome municipal early election.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-Guardian1-6) Described by _The Economist_ as "a talented debater",[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-7) Raggi is the first female mayor of the city. Raggi and her party (Five Star Movement, M5S) came in first place in the first round of voting (5 June 2016) in the Rome mayoral election, garnering over 35 percent of the vote.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Raggi#cite_note-theage-5) In the second round of voting (19 June 2016), Raggi opposed Roberto Giachetti, a member of the Democratic Party (PD) and Vice President of the Chamber of Deputies in the XVII Legislature, who obtained over 24 percent of the vote in first round.
